subject: Aurelia Dedicated sizing / throughput targets & pricing worksheet
messages:
From: Ethan Ward <ethan.ward@aureliacorp.com>
To: dylan_brooks@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-10-10T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Dedicated commit - target TPS and pricing questions

Hi Dylan —

Quick context: Aurelia is evaluating a Redwood Dedicated pool to serve our product search & ranking flows. We ran a small pilot on the hosted API but need guaranteed throughput and predictable unit costs for launch Q1.

We have two traffic shapes:
- Search read (mostly short prompts): peak 450 rps, typical 180 rps (p95 latency target < 200ms)
- Re-ranker (longer context, multi-pass): peak 60 rps, typical 25 rps (p95 < 400ms)

Questions:
1) What Dedicated commit size (GPU count / class) would you recommend to hit sustained 500 rps across both flows with our latency targets?
2) What are the pricing tiers / discounts for 6- and 12-month reserved commits?
3) Can you share load test artifacts / TPS traces to justify the sizing recommendations?

We can share sample traces if useful. Looking for a ballpark today so we can budget.

Thanks —
Ethan
Ethan Ward
Head of Infrastructure, Aurelia Commerce

From: dylan_brooks@redwood.ai
To: Ethan Ward <ethan.ward@aureliacorp.com>, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Cc: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-10-13T11:34:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated commit - target TPS and pricing questions

Thanks Ethan — this is helpful. Quick answers up front, then a plan to validate with numbers:

Initial guidance (ballpark):
- Sizing: 8x H100-equivalent GPUs (shared pool) with autoscale headroom to 10 GPUs should comfortably sustain the 500 rps target across both flows with conservative batching. That assumes optimized batching + prefix KV cache for search.
- SLA: we can target p95 latency SLOs like you describe in Dedicated with an SLA addendum; we'll want to define traffic mix and failure fallbacks in the MA/commit.
- Pricing: 6-month commit: base discount 18% off list for committed GPU-hours; 12-month commit: 25% with additional volume tiers for >24k GPU-hours/month. We can structure a blend with burst credits for short peaks.

Next step: Marissa (perf lead) will run a workload-shaped load test using your representative traces and our Dedicated runtime and share the TPS CSV + Grafana dashboards. That will let us produce a recommended commit size and a compact pricing worksheet (commit, expected unit tokens/sec economics, and proposed discount).

Marissa — can you run two batches: (A) search-dominant mix, (B) re-ranker heavy, both for 30min sustained with 5m ramp and capture p50/p95/p99, GPU utilization, effective tokens/sec, and batch size distribution? Attach traces and a short write-up.

Ethan — do you have a sample request trace or replay logs for the week of Sep 20 we can use? If not, Marissa can use synthetic but will call out assumptions.

Thanks —
Dylan
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
To: dylan_brooks@redwood.ai, Ethan Ward <ethan.ward@aureliacorp.com>
Cc: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-10-15T15:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated commit - target TPS and pricing questions

Ethan / Dylan — attaching results from the Dedicated runtime runs we executed against a replay of the Sep20 trace (90% fidelity to provided samples). Summary below; full CSVs and traces attached.

Summary (30m sustained, 8x H100-equivalent GPUs):
- Mix A (search-dominant, 85% search / 15% re-rank)
  - sustained RPS: 480 avg (peaks 510)
  - p50 latency: 85ms (search), 240ms (re-ranker)
  - p95 latency: 190ms (search), 360ms (re-ranker)
  - GPU util: avg 78% (some batching inefficiency at tail)
  - effective tokens/sec (aggregate): ~1.8M tokens/sec across pool
  - KV cache hit rate: 62% (prefix reuse helped search)

- Mix B (re-ranker heavy, 40% search / 60% re-rank)
  - sustained RPS: 220 avg (peaks 260)
  - p50 latency: 120ms (search), 320ms (re-ranker)
  - p95 latency: 260ms (search), 480ms (re-ranker)
  - GPU util: avg 83% (more steady batching)
  - effective tokens/sec: ~1.6M tokens/sec

Observations / recommendation:
- An 8x H100 pool hits your combined 500rps target in the search-heavy mix with headroom for short bursts but is near capacity for sustained re-ranker-heavy patterns.
- If Aurelia expects >40% sustained re-ranker share, size to 10x H100-equivalent GPUs.
- We recommend configuring prefix KV caching and conservative max_batch (8->12 tokens per batch for search) to keep p95 in the 150-220ms range for search.
- For commit sizing/pricing, the numbers used below assume 8 GPUs sustained (72% util)/month baseline; we included burst credits for 10% of peak minutes.

Attached: 20261015_aurelia_tps_summary.csv (per-second TPS, latencies), loadtest_traces_20261015.zip (perf traces & traces/ spans), grafana_screenshots_aurelia.png

Let me know if you want a cost-per-1k-tokens worksheet and a modeled 6/12-month price table; happy to produce that for procurement.

—Marissa
Perf Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Ethan Ward <ethan.ward@aureliacorp.com>
To: dylan_brooks@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@aureliacorp.com
Date: 2026-10-18T09:27:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated commit - target TPS and pricing questions

Thanks Marissa — that level of detail is perfect. A few procurement-specific follow-ups from our side:

1) Pricing sensitivity: if we commit to an 8-GPU (H100-eq) pool for 12 months, what's the final blended discount you can offer if we also commit to purchase 5TB of model weights hosting and an observability add-on? We're targeting ~28-30% off list.
2) SLA credits: for a 99.9% latency SLO on the search flow, what credit schedule do you propose?
3) Acceptance test: we want a 72-hour acceptance window during which we'll run our replay and verify throughput/latency and have the right to adjust the committed size if the replay shows >10% delta vs the reported numbers. Would you accept that?

Also thumbs up on the recommendation to include burst credits. If you can send a draft worksheet with monthly committed GPU-hours, expected monthly token volumes, and an indicative invoice number, that will help procurement.

—Ethan

From: dylan_brooks@redwood.ai
To: Ethan Ward <ethan.ward@aureliacorp.com>, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Cc: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai, procurement@aureliacorp.com
Date: 2026-10-21T16:35:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated commit - target TPS and pricing questions (pricing worksheet & next steps)

Ethan — thanks. Attached is a first-pass pricing worksheet and the proposed commercial terms. High-level:

- Recommended commit: 8x H100-equivalent GPUs (baseline). Option A (recommended): 8 GPU baseline + burst pool to 10 GPUs. Option B (if >40% re-rank sustained): baseline 10 GPUs.
- Acceptance: we accept a 72-hour acceptance test window tied to your replay; if the measured p95 or sustained RPS is >10% worse than Marissa's reported figures, we will allow a one-time right to resize the baseline without penalty (mutual sign-off).
- Pricing (indicative, USD/month, list = $X / GPU-hour):
  - 6-month commit: blended 20% discount, one-time onboarding credit $5k
  - 12-month commit + model-hosting (5TB) + observability add-on: blended 29% discount and 3 months of burst credits (20% of monthly GPU-hours) included.
- SLA & credits: 99.9% latency SLO for search flow - standard SLA credits apply (sliding scale, up to 25% monthly credit for sustained SLO misses). We'll provide the SLA addendum in the contract.

Next steps:
1) I'll upload the pricing worksheet and a DocuSign-ready MA (with acceptance clause) to the HubSpot deal.
2) Marissa will hand over the CSVs and a short guidance doc for running the 72-hr acceptance replay.
3) Procurement: if you want the deeper unit economics (#tokens / $ / 1k tokens) we can produce a per-route table.

If that reads OK, I'll schedule a short 30-min call between procurement + engineering this week to confirm acceptance test details and finalize the commit length.

Thanks —
Dylan
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
